name: Sputnik 1
objective: The first artificial satellite, launched to test orbital spaceflight.
discoveries: Demonstrated that artificial satellites could be placed in orbit, beginning the Space Age.
objectives: Test orbital spaceflight capability
Demonstrate satellite tracking via radio signal
achievements: First artificial satellite to orbit Earth
Began the Space Age and the Space Race

name: Vostok 1
objective: Carried Yuri Gagarin, the first human to travel into space and orbit the Earth.
discoveries: Proved that humans could survive spaceflight and orbital conditions.
objectives: Achieve the first crewed orbital spaceflight
achievements: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space and in orbit
Completed one orbit of Earth in 108 minutes

name: Mariner 10
objective: First mission to visit Mercury, using a gravity assist from Venus.
discoveries: Returned the first close-up images of Mercury's cratered surface.
objectives: Perform the first flyby exploration of Mercury
Test a gravity-assist trajectory using Venus
achievements: First spacecraft to use a planetary gravity assist
First close-up images of Mercury's cratered surface
Three flybys of Mercury between 1974–1975

name: Venera Program
objective: A series of probes to study Venus, including the first landings on another planet.
discoveries: Venera 9 returned the first images from the surface of another planet.
objectives: Study Venus's atmosphere and surface
Achieve the first landing on another planet
achievements: Venera 7 was the first spacecraft to soft-land on another planet (1970)
Venera 9 returned the first images from another planet's surface (1975)

name: Voyager 1 & 2
objective: Grand tour of the outer planets, later continuing into interstellar space.
discoveries: Detailed imagery of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune; discovered active volcanoes on Io and geysers on Triton; Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object.
objectives: Conduct a 'grand tour' flyby of the outer planets
Study interstellar space beyond the heliosphere
achievements: Discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io
Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object
Both probes have crossed into interstellar space

name: Voyager 2
objective: The only spacecraft to have flown by Uranus and Neptune.
discoveries: Returned the only close-up data we have of Uranus and Neptune, including their rings and moons.
objectives: Extend the grand tour to Uranus and Neptune
achievements: Only spacecraft to fly by Uranus and Neptune
Discovered active geysers on Neptune's moon Triton

name: Magellan
objective: Mapped the surface of Venus using radar to see through its thick clouds.
discoveries: Produced the most detailed global map of Venus's surface, revealing widespread volcanism.
objectives: Map Venus's surface using synthetic aperture radar
achievements: Produced the most detailed global radar map of Venus at the time
Revealed extensive volcanic resurfacing

name: Hubble Space Telescope
objective: A space-based observatory studying the universe across visible, ultraviolet, and near-infrared light.
discoveries: Helped determine the rate of the universe's expansion, imaged distant galaxies, and captured iconic nebula imagery.
objectives: Observe the universe from above Earth's atmosphere across ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light
achievements: Helped refine the Hubble Constant (rate of cosmic expansion)
Captured the Hubble Deep Field
Studied countless galaxies, nebulae, and exoplanet atmospheres over 30+ years

name: Galileo
objective: Studied Jupiter and its moons in detail over an eight-year orbital mission.
discoveries: Found strong evidence of a subsurface ocean on Europa and studied Io's active volcanism up close.
objectives: Orbit Jupiter and study its atmosphere, moons, and magnetosphere
Deploy an atmospheric entry probe into Jupiter
achievements: Found strong evidence of a subsurface ocean on Europa
Directly studied Io's volcanism up close
Deployed a probe into Jupiter's atmosphere

name: Akatsuki
objective: Studies the atmosphere and weather of Venus.
discoveries: Discovered a massive stationary gravity wave in Venus's atmosphere.
objectives: Study Venus's atmospheric circulation and weather
achievements: Recovered from a 2010 orbit-insertion failure to achieve orbit in 2015
Discovered a massive stationary gravity wave in Venus's atmosphere

name: Cassini-Huygens
objective: Studied Saturn, its rings, and its moons; the Huygens probe landed on Titan.
discoveries: Found geysers on Enceladus, mapped Titan's methane lakes, and revealed fine structure in Saturn's rings.
objectives: Conduct a multi-year orbital study of Saturn, its rings, and its moons
Deliver the Huygens probe to Titan's surface
achievements: Found active water-ice geysers erupting from Enceladus
Landed Huygens on Titan — the first landing in the outer Solar System
Revealed fine structure in Saturn's rings
Deliberately deorbited into Saturn to protect potentially habitable moons

name: International Space Station
objective: A continuously crewed research laboratory in low Earth orbit.
discoveries: Enabled long-duration research on human physiology and countless microgravity experiments.
objectives: Provide a continuously crewed microgravity research laboratory in low Earth orbit
achievements: Continuously crewed since November 2000
Long-duration human physiology research supporting future deep-space missions
International collaboration across five partner space agencies

name: Viking 1 & 2
objective: First successful landings on Mars to return images from the surface.
discoveries: Returned the first color images from the Martian surface and conducted early searches for signs of life.
objectives: Achieve the first successful Mars landings
Search for signs of life in Martian soil
achievements: First successful landings and images from the Martian surface
Conducted the first biological experiments searching for life on another planet

name: InSight
objective: Studied the deep interior of Mars, including marsquakes.
discoveries: Detected hundreds of marsquakes, revealing details of Mars's crust, mantle, and core.
objectives: Study Mars's deep interior using a seismometer and a heat-flow probe
achievements: Detected hundreds of marsquakes
Revealed the size and structure of Mars's crust, mantle, and core

name: Curiosity Rover
objective: Explores Gale Crater to study Mars's past habitability.
discoveries: Confirmed ancient lakebed environments and detected organic molecules in Martian rocks.
objectives: Assess whether Gale Crater ever offered conditions favorable for microbial life
achievements: Confirmed ancient lakebed and river environments
Detected complex organic molecules in Martian rocks
Measured seasonal methane fluctuations of debated origin

name: New Horizons
objective: First mission to fly by Pluto and explore the Kuiper Belt.
discoveries: Returned the first detailed images of Pluto and Charon, revealing Tombaugh Regio.
objectives: Perform the first flyby reconnaissance of Pluto and Charon
Explore additional Kuiper Belt objects
achievements: First detailed images of Pluto, revealing Tombaugh Regio
First close flyby of a Kuiper Belt object (Arrokoth, 2019)

name: Juno
objective: Studies Jupiter's composition, gravity field, magnetic field, and polar magnetosphere.
discoveries: Revealed complex polar cyclones and provided new data on Jupiter's deep atmosphere.
objectives: Study Jupiter's composition, gravity field, magnetic field, and polar magnetosphere from a polar orbit
achievements: Revealed complex, long-lived polar cyclones
Returned new data on Jupiter's deep atmosphere and interior structure

name: Perseverance Rover
objective: Searches for signs of ancient life and collects samples for future return to Earth.
discoveries: Collected rock core samples in Jezero Crater and tested oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere.
objectives: Search for signs of ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater
Collect rock and soil samples for future return to Earth
Test oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere via the MOXIE instrument
achievements: Collected the first rock core samples cached for eventual return to Earth
Demonstrated oxygen production from Martian CO2 via MOXIE
Deployed Ingenuity, the first powered flight on another planet

name: BepiColombo
objective: A joint mission to study Mercury's surface, interior, and magnetosphere.
discoveries: Returned new flyby imagery of Mercury en route to orbital insertion.
objectives: Study Mercury's surface composition, interior structure, and magnetosphere using two science orbiters
achievements: Returned new flyby imagery of Mercury en route to orbital insertion
Carries two complementary orbiters — ESA's MPO and JAXA's Mio

name: James Webb Space Telescope
objective: An infrared observatory studying the earliest galaxies, star formation, and exoplanet atmospheres.
discoveries: Imaged some of the most distant known galaxies and analyzed exoplanet atmospheric compositions.
objectives: Observe the universe primarily in infrared light to study the earliest galaxies, star and planet formation, and exoplanet atmospheres
achievements: Imaged some of the most distant known galaxies
Directly analyzed exoplanet atmospheric compositions
Operates from the Sun-Earth L2 point

name: MESSENGER
objective: First spacecraft to orbit Mercury, mapping its surface and studying its composition, magnetic field, and thin exosphere.
discoveries: Confirmed water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters and produced the first complete map of Mercury.
objectives: Achieve the first orbital mission to Mercury
Map Mercury's surface composition and magnetic field
achievements: First spacecraft to orbit Mercury
Confirmed water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters
Produced the first complete global map of Mercury

name: Apollo Program
objective: Landed the first humans on the Moon and returned them safely to Earth across six successful crewed landings.
discoveries: Returned 382 kg of lunar samples and deployed instruments that transformed understanding of the Moon's origin and geology.
objectives: Land humans on the Moon and return them safely to Earth
Conduct lunar surface science across multiple landing sites
achievements: Apollo 11 (1969): first crewed Moon landing, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin
Six successful crewed landings between 1969–1972
Returned 382 kg of lunar samples, still studied today

name: Aryabhata
objective: India's first satellite, built to test India's satellite-building capability and carry X-ray astronomy and aeronomy experiments.
discoveries: Demonstrated India's capability to design and build a scientific satellite; launched with Soviet assistance.
objectives: Test India's satellite design and fabrication capability
Carry X-ray astronomy and aeronomy experiments
achievements: India's first satellite
Established the foundation of India's satellite programme

name: Rohini Satellite Series (RS-1)
objective: India's first satellite launched by an Indian-built rocket, the SLV-3, establishing indigenous orbital launch capability.
discoveries: Made India the seventh country to independently place a satellite into orbit using its own launch vehicle.
objectives: Demonstrate India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle, SLV-3
achievements: First satellite launched into orbit by an Indian-built rocket

name: PSLV — Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle
objective: ISRO's reliable workhorse rocket, used for Earth observation, navigation, and India's interplanetary missions.
discoveries: Enabled Chandrayaan-1, the Mars Orbiter Mission, and a record-setting single-launch deployment of 104 satellites in 2017.
objectives: Provide reliable, reusable launch capability for Earth observation, navigation, and interplanetary missions
achievements: Launched Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission
Set a record for most satellites launched in a single mission (104, in 2017)

name: GSLV — Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle
objective: Developed to carry heavier payloads to geostationary transfer orbit using an indigenous cryogenic upper stage.
discoveries: Enabled India's heavier communication and navigation satellite launches, including Chandrayaan-2.
objectives: Carry heavier satellites to geostationary transfer orbit using indigenous cryogenic technology
achievements: Launched Chandrayaan-2
Enabled India's larger communication and weather satellites

name: Chandrayaan-1
objective: India's first lunar mission, designed to map the Moon's surface chemistry and mineralogy from orbit.
discoveries: Instruments aboard Chandrayaan-1 contributed to confirming the presence of water molecules on the lunar surface.
objectives: Map the Moon's surface chemistry and mineralogy from orbit
Deploy the Moon Impact Probe to study the lunar surface at close range
achievements: India's first lunar mission
Contributed to the confirmation of water molecules on the lunar surface
Produced detailed mineralogical maps of the Moon

name: Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
objective: India's first interplanetary mission, designed to demonstrate technologies for interplanetary travel and study Mars's atmosphere and surface.
discoveries: Made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit, and the first nation in the world to succeed on its very first attempt.
objectives: Demonstrate technologies required for interplanetary missions
Study Mars's atmosphere, surface, and mineralogy from orbit
achievements: India's first interplanetary mission
Reached Mars orbit on its first attempt
Operated far beyond its original 6-month design life, until 2022

name: AstroSat
objective: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, studying celestial sources simultaneously in X-ray, optical, and ultraviolet light.
discoveries: Enabled simultaneous multi-wavelength studies of neutron stars, black holes, and galaxies.
objectives: Study celestial X-ray sources, and simultaneously observe them in optical/UV light
achievements: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength astronomy satellite
Continues to contribute to studies of neutron stars, black holes, and active galaxies

name: Chandrayaan-2
objective: A lunar orbiter, lander (Vikram), and rover (Pragyan) mission; the orbiter succeeded fully while the lander experienced a hard landing.
discoveries: The orbiter continues to return valuable lunar science data; the lander outcome directly informed Chandrayaan-3's redesigned descent system.
objectives: Orbit the Moon and conduct remote-sensing science
Achieve a soft landing and deploy a rover near the lunar south pole
achievements: Orbiter successfully inserted into lunar orbit and remains operational
Provided detailed data that directly informed the successful Chandrayaan-3 landing

name: Chandrayaan-3
objective: Achieve a safe, soft landing near the Moon's south pole and operate a rover to study the lunar surface in situ.
discoveries: Made India the first country to land near the lunar south pole and the fourth nation overall to achieve a soft lunar landing; the Pragyan rover confirmed sulfur and other elements in the lunar soil.
objectives: Demonstrate a safe, soft landing near the lunar south pole
Demonstrate rover mobility on the lunar surface
Conduct in-situ scientific experiments
achievements: First successful soft landing near the lunar south pole by any nation
India became the fourth country to achieve a soft lunar landing
Pragyan rover conducted in-situ chemical analysis, confirming sulfur and other elements

timeline_stages.description: Launched on 14 July 2023 aboard an LVM3 rocket from Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
Entered lunar orbit in early August 2023.
The Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.
The Pragyan rover conducted in-situ analysis of lunar soil composition.
Lander and rover completed planned operations during the two-week lunar day before entering sleep mode for the lunar night.

name: Aditya-L1
objective: India's first dedicated solar observation mission, positioned near the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point for continuous, uninterrupted observation of the Sun.
discoveries: Provides continuous observations of the solar corona, solar wind, and space weather phenomena from seven onboard instruments.
objectives: Continuously observe the Sun's corona, chromosphere, and solar wind from the L1 vantage point
Study the origins and propagation of coronal mass ejections and space weather
achievements: India's first dedicated solar mission
Successfully inserted into a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point in January 2024

timeline_stages.description: Launched on 2 September 2023 aboard a PSLV rocket.
Raised its orbit around Earth in stages before departing for L1.
Traveled roughly 1.5 million km toward the Sun-Earth L1 point.
Entered a halo orbit around L1 in January 2024.
Continuously observes the Sun with seven scientific payloads.

name: XPoSat
objective: India's first dedicated X-ray polarimetry mission, studying the polarization of X-rays from extreme cosmic sources such as black holes and neutron stars.
discoveries: Studies the geometry and emission mechanisms of X-ray sources that cannot be fully understood from brightness and spectrum alone.
objectives: Measure the polarization of X-rays from bright astronomical sources
Study the geometry and radiation mechanisms of black holes and neutron stars
achievements: India's first X-ray polarimetry mission
One of only a small number of such missions flown worldwide

name: Gaganyaan
objective: India's programme to independently launch astronauts into low Earth orbit aboard an Indian-built crewed spacecraft.
discoveries: Uncrewed test flights and crew-escape-system tests are underway ahead of a planned crewed mission — see ISRO's official page for the current schedule.
objectives: Independently launch Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit and return them safely
Validate crew module, life-support, and abort systems through uncrewed test flights
achievements: Conducted crew escape system and uncrewed test flight demonstrations

name: Rosetta
objective: First mission to orbit a comet nucleus and deploy a lander (Philae) onto its surface.
discoveries: Philae achieved the first-ever landing on a comet nucleus; Rosetta studied the comet's composition and activity for two years as it approached the Sun.
objectives: Orbit and closely study a comet nucleus over an extended period
Land a probe on the comet's surface
achievements: First spacecraft to orbit a comet nucleus
Philae achieved the first landing on a comet
Detected organic molecules and studied the comet's water composition

related_cosmos.label: Small Bodies of the Solar System

name: Gaia
objective: Precisely map the positions, distances, and motions of over a billion stars to build the most detailed 3D map of the Milky Way.
discoveries: Produced the most precise stellar catalog ever made, reshaping understanding of the Milky Way's structure, history, and formation.
objectives: Precisely measure the position, distance, and motion of over a billion stars
achievements: Produced the most precise 3D map of the Milky Way to date
Enabled new studies of galactic structure, star clusters, and stellar evolution

name: Euclid
objective: Map the geometry of the 'dark universe' by surveying billions of galaxies to study dark matter and dark energy.
discoveries: Building a 3D map of the large-scale structure of the universe across more than a third of the sky.
objectives: Survey billions of galaxies to map the large-scale structure of the universe
Constrain the properties of dark matter and dark energy
achievements: Began its wide-field survey of the extragalactic sky
Early observations have already resolved fine structure in galaxy clusters

name: Solar Orbiter
objective: Study the Sun and inner heliosphere from close range and out-of-ecliptic vantage points, in collaboration with NASA.
discoveries: Returned the closest-ever images of the Sun at the time of launch and observed 'campfires' — small-scale flare-like brightenings across the solar surface.
objectives: Observe the Sun at close range and from high solar latitudes not visible from Earth
achievements: Returned the closest-ever images of the Sun at the time
Discovered widespread small-scale 'campfire' flare-like events

name: Mars Express
objective: ESA's first mission to Mars, studying the atmosphere, surface, and subsurface for over two decades.
discoveries: Found strong evidence of subsurface water ice near the Martian poles and produced detailed high-resolution maps of the planet.
objectives: Study Mars's atmosphere, surface, and subsurface from orbit
achievements: Found strong evidence of subsurface water ice near the Martian poles
One of the longest continuously operating Mars orbiters

name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
objective: Study trace gases like methane in the Martian atmosphere and relay communications for a future life-detection rover.
discoveries: Provided the most sensitive measurements yet of trace atmospheric gases on Mars.
objectives: Precisely measure trace gases in the Martian atmosphere, including methane
Serve as a communications relay for surface missions
achievements: Provided the most sensitive trace-gas measurements of the Martian atmosphere to date

name: JUICE — Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer
objective: Study Jupiter's system with a focus on three icy moons — Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa — as potential ocean worlds.
discoveries: En route to Jupiter, with arrival expected in the early 2030s after a series of gravity-assist flybys.
objectives: Characterize Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa as potential ocean worlds
Study Jupiter's atmosphere, magnetosphere, and moon system as an archetype for gas giants
achievements: Successfully launched and began its multi-year cruise to Jupiter

name: Herschel Space Observatory
objective: The largest infrared space telescope of its time, studying star formation and galaxy evolution.
discoveries: Discovered water vapor in protoplanetary disks and studied the coldest, earliest stages of star formation.
objectives: Observe the universe in far-infrared and submillimeter light to study cold star-forming regions
achievements: Discovered water vapor around forming planetary systems
Studied the earliest, coldest stages of star formation in unprecedented detail

name: Hayabusa
objective: First mission to land on an asteroid and return a surface sample to Earth.
discoveries: Returned the first asteroid surface samples to Earth in 2010, despite major technical failures during the mission.
objectives: Land on an asteroid and collect a surface sample
Return the sample to Earth for laboratory study
achievements: First asteroid sample-return mission
Overcame multiple major spacecraft failures to return home

related_cosmos.label: Small Bodies of the Solar System

name: Hayabusa2
objective: Return samples from asteroid Ryugu, including subsurface material obtained via an artificial impact experiment.
discoveries: Returned subsurface asteroid samples for the first time, containing organic molecules and amino acids relevant to the origins of life's building blocks.
objectives: Return both surface and subsurface samples from asteroid Ryugu
Study a carbon-rich asteroid linked to the origins of water and organics on Earth
achievements: Returned both surface and subsurface asteroid samples
Created an artificial crater using a small explosive impactor
Returned samples containing amino acids and organic compounds

related_cosmos.label: Small Bodies of the Solar System

name: SLIM — Smart Lander for Investigating Moon
objective: Demonstrate high-precision 'pinpoint' lunar landing technology, targeting a landing accuracy of around 100 meters.
discoveries: Achieved a highly precise lunar landing, though it touched down at an unintended angle; made Japan the fifth nation to soft-land on the Moon.
objectives: Demonstrate pinpoint lunar landing accuracy for future exploration missions
achievements: Demonstrated high-precision lunar landing technology
Made Japan the fifth nation to achieve a soft lunar landing

name: Kaguya (SELENE)
objective: Study the Moon's origin and evolution through detailed mapping of its surface, gravity field, and environment.
discoveries: Produced detailed topographic and gravity maps of the Moon and captured high-definition Earth-rise footage.
objectives: Map the Moon's surface topography, gravity field, and mineral composition
achievements: Produced detailed topographic and gravity maps of the Moon
Captured widely-viewed high-definition Earth-rise footage

name: MMX — Martian Moons eXploration
objective: Explore Mars's moons Phobos and Deimos and return a sample from Phobos to help determine their origin.
discoveries: Mission in development; see JAXA's official page for the current planned launch date.
objectives: Determine whether Phobos and Deimos are captured asteroids or debris from a Mars impact
Return a sample from Phobos to Earth

name: Chang'e 4
objective: Achieve the first-ever soft landing on the Moon's far side and study its geology with the Yutu-2 rover.
discoveries: First spacecraft to soft-land on and directly explore the lunar far side, relaying communications via the Queqiao satellite at the Earth-Moon L2 point.
objectives: Achieve the first soft landing on the lunar far side
Study the geology of the South Pole-Aitken basin with a rover
achievements: First soft landing on the Moon's far side
Yutu-2 has driven farther across the lunar surface than any previous rover

name: Chang'e 5
objective: Collect and return lunar samples to Earth — the first lunar sample-return mission since the 1970s.
discoveries: Returned about 1.7 kg of lunar samples from a previously unsampled region, revealing surprisingly recent volcanic activity on the Moon.
objectives: Collect lunar samples from a young volcanic region and return them to Earth
achievements: First lunar sample return since the Soviet Luna 24 mission in 1976
Samples revealed volcanic activity roughly 2 billion years ago, younger than previously known

name: Tianwen-1
objective: Orbit, land on, and rove across Mars in a single mission — combining three mission types in one launch.
discoveries: Made China the second country to successfully operate a rover on Mars, via the Zhurong rover exploring Utopia Planitia.
objectives: Combine orbital reconnaissance with a surface landing and rover in a single mission
achievements: Combined orbiter, lander, and rover in a single mission
Zhurong rover explored Utopia Planitia
Made China the second nation to land and operate a rover on Mars

name: Canadarm
objective: A robotic arm developed for the Space Shuttle to deploy, capture, and manipulate payloads in orbit.
discoveries: Flew on 90 Space Shuttle missions, becoming one of the most recognized contributions of the Canadian space programme.
objectives: Provide robotic payload deployment and capture capability for the Space Shuttle
achievements: Flew on 90 Space Shuttle missions
Enabled satellite deployment, capture, and repair, including Hubble servicing missions

name: Canadarm2
objective: A larger, more capable robotic arm permanently installed on the ISS for assembly, maintenance, and cargo capture.
discoveries: Essential to ISS assembly and continues to capture uncrewed cargo spacecraft arriving at the station.
objectives: Support ISS assembly, maintenance, and visiting-vehicle capture
achievements: Essential to the assembly of the ISS
Continues to capture uncrewed cargo spacecraft arriving at the station

name: Hope Mars Mission (Al Amal)
objective: The UAE's first interplanetary mission, studying the Martian atmosphere and weather to build a complete picture of its daily and seasonal cycles.
discoveries: Provided a first-of-its-kind complete picture of the Martian atmosphere across all times of day, made possible by its unique wide orbit.
objectives: Study the Martian atmosphere's daily and seasonal weather cycles from a wide, unique orbit
achievements: UAE's first interplanetary mission
First Arab nation to reach Mars
Fifth agency in the world to successfully reach Mars orbit

name: Luna Programme
objective: A series of Soviet uncrewed missions to the Moon, achieving numerous firsts in lunar exploration.
discoveries: Luna 2 was the first spacecraft to reach the Moon's surface (1959); Luna 3 returned the first images of the Moon's far side; Luna 9 achieved the first soft landing on another world (1966).
objectives: Achieve the first uncrewed exploration of the Moon via flyby, impact, orbit, and landing
achievements: Luna 2: first spacecraft to reach the Moon's surface (1959)
Luna 3: first images of the Moon's far side (1959)
Luna 9: first soft landing on another world (1966)

name: Mir Space Station
objective: A modular space station launched under the Soviet Union and operated by Russia's Roscosmos after 1992, hosting long-duration crewed missions as a precursor to the ISS.
discoveries: Hosted the longest single continuous human spaceflight on record (Valeri Polyakov, 437 days) and pioneered long-duration spaceflight techniques.
objectives: Provide a long-duration crewed research platform in low Earth orbit
achievements: Longest single continuous human spaceflight on record at the time (437 days)
Pioneered long-duration spaceflight and life-support techniques later used on the ISS

name: Soyuz Programme
objective: A long-running family of crewed spacecraft that has carried cosmonauts, astronauts, and international partners to orbit since 1967.
discoveries: The longest continuously operated crewed spaceflight programme in history, and for nearly a decade was the sole means of crewed access to the ISS for all partner nations.
objectives: Provide reliable crewed transport to Earth orbit and the ISS
achievements: Longest continuously operated crewed spaceflight programme in history
Sole means of crewed ISS access for all partner nations from 2011–2020
